title: When Does Divide and Conquer Work for Long Context LLM? A Noise Decomposition Framework
selection_reason: The paper evaluates divide-and-conquer long-context LLM processing and, beyond task fidelity, explicitly derives serving-cost implications: Appendix N models parallel-worker wall-clock latency as one chunk-worker pass plus one manager pass and states when this can beat single-pass inference. The advantage depends on available concurrency and network/aggregation overhead, and is modeled rather than established by end-to-end latency measurements; the concrete inference-latency connection warrants carrying it forward.
